segment.description: J. Percy Priest Reservoir itself — the 14,200-acre USACE impoundment near east Nashville on the Stones River, in Davidson, Rutherford, and Wilson counties (catalog). TWRA documents an entirely warmwater fishery: largemouth/smallmouth/spotted bass, crappie, hybrid/striped/white/yellow bass, catfish, rock bass, and sunfish — trout are not mentioned on TWRA's reservoir page. The prior composite pass's 'warmwater stocking events' flag is corrected here: the trout rows associated with this name are RAINBOW TROUT stocked in the TAILWATER reach below the dam (Stones River), a separate catalog water, not in the lake.
segment.boundaries: USACE reservoir pool behind J. Percy Priest Dam; catalog counties Davidson, Rutherford, Wilson. The winter trout stocking site 'J. Percy Priest TW / Stones River' (Davidson Co.) is the dam tailwater below the lake, outside this segment.

coldSource.notes: TWRA: 'The US Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) owns and operates J. Percy Priest Reservoir' — 'a 14,200-acre impoundment located near east Nashville'. No cold-release characterization is documented for the dam. The tailwater below the dam receives winter rainbow trout stockings (TWRA Region 2 tailwater list: 'J. Percy Priest Dam, Stones River - Rainbow - December through March - Statewide Regulations'; 2026 workbook rows 1/9/2026, 02/13/2026, TBD 12/2026 under 'J. Percy Priest TW / Stones River') — that program belongs to the tailwater segment, not this lake segment.

holdover.detail: No trout fishery is documented in the lake itself: TWRA's reservoir page lists no trout among its species, the 2026 stocking schedule/workbook contains no in-lake trout stocking location, and the only trout program bearing this name is the December-March put-take rainbow stocking in the Stones River tailwater below the dam (different segment).

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documented. TWRA's species list for the reservoir is entirely warmwater (bass, crappie, striped/hybrid bass, catfish, sunfish).

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Warm 14,200-acre USACE flood-control reservoir whose documented fishery is entirely warmwater; TWRA confines the associated trout program to a December-March rainbow stocking in the tailwater below the dam, which by design is not year-round lake habitat.
